title: I made this: a zero-HUD browser survival game inside a damaged zero-g Lifeboat (free on itch.io) (Heavily Inspired by TinCan)
author: CaptainSuckie
selftext:
Hey guys, human text here before the AI-wall of text. 

I hope you enjoy my game, if you liked the game TinCan as much as I did, you should find it pretty similar. 

Looking forward to your feedback! Thanks gang.

  


\*\*Play free in your browser (desktop mouse/keyboard or gamepad):\*\* [https://flaccidnoise.itch.io/stay-with-the-lifeboat](https://flaccidnoise.itch.io/stay-with-the-lifeboat)



\*Stay With the Lifeboat\* is a first-person zero-g survival game built in TypeScript and Three.js.



\*\*What it is:\*\*

\- \*\*Short playable Escape tutorial, then no hand-holding:\*\* You start on a failing station learning zero-g movement, gripping, opening panels, and launching. Once you clear the Station, every on-screen overlay disappears — no markers, no quest log, no HUD.

\- \*\*Physical Flight Manual:\*\* Power budgets, Cabin maps, Part types, and emergency procedures (fires, hull breaches, EVA, orbital burns, docking, calling for rescue) are all printed in the physical Manual strapped beside the Pilot seat.

\- \*\*Hands-on repairs & power triage:\*\* Unbolt Access panels with a Driver, probe Parts with a Multimeter, swap or patch failing components, balance solar/fuel cell/battery draw, go outside on EVA to fix exterior Systems, and either dock at an Outpost or hold out for Rescue.



\*\*Heads up before playing:\*\*

\- Desktop browser only (mouse + keyboard, or gamepad — no touch controls).

\- Use the Fullscreen button on the embed (or inside Settings).

\- If zero-g rolling feels rough at first, Settings has \*\*Auto-roll\*\* and \*\*Floor gravity\*\* toggles.



Happy to answer questions about the sim or hear how your first Run went.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/CaptainSuckie could you add more about how AI fit into your development process? Just mentioning that AI was used doesn't cut it. Under Rule 4, promotional posts need to contribute something by discussing how the game was actually made. Otherwise the sub gets buried in ads. If there's no update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: CaptainSuckie
replies.body: Good call. I just updated the post with a breakdown of the AI workflow, the sim/renderer split, the Blender Python asset pipeline, and the automated Playwright/pre-commit guardrails we had to build to keep agent output from drifting. Let me know if you want me to expand on any part of it.
